text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.3 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking: This is a classic public goods game where keeping a token nets me 1, but contributing only returns 0.3 to me while spreading 0.9 to others—so self-interest says keep everything, even though full group cooperation would yield the highest collective payoff.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This is a public goods game where each contributed token returns 0.3 to each of 4 members, so contributing gives back less to the individual than it costs, making zero contribution the dominant self-interested strategy even though full cooperation maximizes the group's total payoff.

Since I'm playing for my own points, I'll compromise by starting with a moderate contribution like 10 to signal cooperation and test how others respond, rather than going fully selfish or fully altruistic.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking: This is a public goods game with an MPCR of 0.3, meaning each token I keep is worth more to me individually (1) than each token I contribute (0.3 back to self), even though contributing benefits the group more overall. The selfishly dominant move is to keep everything, though I'm weighing whether a cooperative gesture might be worthwhile.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking: This is a public goods game where contributing to the group multiplies value but spreads it across members, so individually keeping tokens private is the dominant selfish strategy even though full cooperation maximizes total payoff. I'm weighing whether to play purely rational-selfish or lean toward some cooperation given the repeated 10-round structure with unknown other players.

calls.text: Round 2 of 10. Last round you put 0 tokens in the group account, it received 10 in total, and you got 23 points.

reply.thinking: Round 2 is similar — contributing costs me since the return is only 0.3 per token, even though others contributed 10 total last round. The dominant strategy still favors keeping everything, though with 10 rounds there's room for reciprocity signals later. For now I'll stick with contributing 0.

reply.thinking: In round 1, my 10 points check out as 13 total, confirming others contributed nothing to the group. Since contributing only returns a fraction back to me individually, the rational move given everyone else's zero contribution is to also contribute zero in round 2.

Given contributing only returns 0.3 per token to me versus 0.9 to others, I'm leaning toward staying selfish and keeping 0.
